title: Two Tables, Two Keys
description: An in-app notification and its matching outbox email are two separate records of the same event, tracked independently — one is not secretly a view of the other.
successCondition: Book a shipment (which both creates a Notification row and a MockMessage row of channel email). After waiting past the queue delay, using `npm run db:psql`, confirm the notifications row's id and the mock_messages row's id are two entirely different UUIDs — there is no shared primary key or foreign key column linking the two tables together (inspect \d notifications and \d mock_messages in psql to confirm neither table references the other).
hints: prisma/schema.prisma's Notification and MockMessage models are independent — both are written by the same notify() call, but the schema itself never relates one to the other.

You can only correlate the two rows after the fact by matching userId/to and roughly by createdAt, exactly the way a real support engineer manually cross-referencing an outbox against an inbox would have to.
